messages:
alexa-support: hey team, escalated issue from Acme: their CI started failing after we published a v2 tagged release of the go sdk, they see a 401 from the go proxy when `go get`ing the module :confused:

sam-ops: can you paste the error & their go.mod / go env?

alexa-support: pasted from customer: 
```
$ GOMAXPROCS=8 go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0
go: downloading github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0: reading github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/go.mod at revision v2.0.0: unauthorized: 401 response from https://goproxy.io: GET https://goproxy.io/github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/@v/v2.0.0.mod
```
and their go.mod (snip):
```
module github.com/acme/app

require (
    github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
)
```
and their detected module upstream shows module path: `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` (v1-style) in the repo's go.mod at tag v2.0.0

mike-eng: hmm two things could be happening: 1) upstream repo's go.mod wasn't updated to v2 module path (should end with /v2) so the tag is semantically inconsistent; 2) the proxy is returning 401 which suggests repo is private or GOPROXY/Auth issues. Which one is blocking?

julia-dev: agree. if upstream tag v2.0.0 still has `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` (no /v2) then the module download will fail for clients requiring semver-compatible import path. The consumer should `require github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 v2.0.0` and the upstream repo go.mod must have `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`.

sam-ops: customer says they can `git clone` and `go build` locally (with GOPRIVATE set) but CI (which uses the public goproxy) fails. So the 401 is from the proxy because the proxy attempted to fetch metadata and couldn't due to access. They are using organization's internal repo though; might need GOPRIVATE or token.

alexa-support: customer attached their CI config: they do `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0` on CI runner with no GOPRIVATE set.

mike-eng: two possible remediation paths: quick workaround: instruct CI to set `GOPRIVATE=github.com/redwood-inference/*` or use `GOPROXY=direct` in CI. Longer fix: publish a v2 tag that matches module path (update go.mod to module .../v2) and push v2.0.1 so consumers can `require .../v2 v2.0.1` cleanly.

julia-dev: adding concrete snippets: 
Workaround (CI):
```
export GOPRIVATE=github.com/redwood-inference/*
export GOPROXY=direct
go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0
```
Recommended proper fix (maintainers):
1) update repo `go.mod` to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`
2) tag `v2.0.1` and push
3) update docs to show import path `/v2`

sam-ops: also note: if maintainers prefer to keep v1 path in repo, they must not use v2 tags. Mixing v2 tag names with v1 module path causes confusing failures.

alexa-support: suggested message to customer: try the CI workaround and if they want us to coordinate with engineering we can ask eng to re-tag v2.0.1. They asked for our actions.

mike-eng: @deploy-bot can you create an incident card for eng-runtime to look at the published tag metadata? include reproduction steps and the customer's CI log.

deploy-bot: created INC-2026: "go-sdk v2 tag: module path mismatch causing CI go get 401" assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2. link: https://redwood-internal/INC-2026

julia-dev: i'll volunteer to prepare a quick repro: create a tiny repo with v2 tag but v1 module path to show exact `go get` behavior, will paste steps shortly.

alexa-support: customer tried the workaround and CI passed when GOPROXY=direct set. they've accepted that as temporary. asked we let them know when we push corrected tag. I'll follow up. :thumbsup:
